purpose: Teach: 難く/突い/自分勝手/思案/一昔/仕草/相次ぐ/注ぎ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは別れ難く感じる人でいらした
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father was someone it was hard to part from.
lines.style: Quiet, remembering. Slow careful phrasing. Gentle weight on each phrase like placing stones in water. Gaze distant, slightly inward.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、孫を軽く突いて笑わせていらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—Grandpa used to give the grandchildren a little poke and make them laugh, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm recollection, almost singing the words. Gentle rhythm. A soft laugh threading underneath. Speaking to Hiroshi with the ease of sixty years together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは自分勝手な振る舞いを許されなかった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father wasn't allowed to be selfish—even once.
lines.style: Measured tone, each word deliberate. A pause before 'selfish' like the weight of that restriction. Sad acceptance underneath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、人生の岐路を思案されてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, he used to think about life's crossroads, didn't he, dear? When he was young.
lines.style: Tender curiosity. Reaching back toward him. A gentle lift at the end—not quite a question, more an invitation to nod together. Soft exhale.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはもう一昔前の方になられた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father belonged to another era already.
lines.style: Quiet finality without harshness. A long, slow breath through the phrase. Small sadness—not tragic, just the way time moves. Trailing off gently.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、武士道的な仕草が美しかったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, his bearing had that beautiful samurai discipline about it, didn't it, dear?
lines.style: Admiring, almost tender. Savoring the memory of his posture, his restraint. A small smile in the voice. Speaking as though Hiroshi might see him that way again.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、不幸な出来事が相次ぐ年もあった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, there were years when one misfortune followed another.
lines.style: Heavier breath. Speaking more slowly, with weight. A pause before 'misfortune' as if touching something old. Voice stays steady but carries the load.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お酒を注ぎ合っていらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, when he was young, the two of you would pour sake for each other, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warmth returning. A small smile breaking through. Speaking close, intimate. Exhale with affection on 'sake'—the shared ritual of it. Gentle, present.
